S57.01.note: Whether a search runs on a given turn is decided by the model and the plan, so the tester may need to repeat the request.
steps: On the chat screen, click the message box and type /search latest AI news.
Press Send.
Watch the reply: a tool row shows 'Search the web' or 'Searched the web' and a 'Web search' card lists the results.
Click the 'Used tools' row to expand it and check that the searches and their sources are listed.
S57.01.where: Chat screen > message box > type /search latest AI news > Send. The web search also runs on its own when the model decides it needs current information.

S57.02.note: The fetch row text is built from the host name, so the exact words depend on the address used.
steps: Click the message box and paste a full page address such as https://example.com.
Type: read this page and tell me what it says.
Press Send.
Look for a tool row that reads 'Fetching' followed by the host name, then check that the reply uses the page's content.
S57.02.where: Chat screen > message box > paste a page address (https://...) and ask 'read this page and tell me what it says' > Send.

S57.03.note: The plan says this is unfinished (switch-on of the url-fetch description in routing-policies.json is pending) and I found no user control for opening a cited PDF, Office file or page by reference; searched apps/web for the fetch tool name and the source-reader wording and found only the fetch tool.

S57.04.note: The search tool row has no fixed visible name in the code I read, so it may appear under its raw tool name.
steps: Click + and choose Add photos & files, then attach two or more files.
Type a question such as: which of these files mentions invoices?
Press Send.
Look for a tool row for the file search and check that the reply names matching files or shows snippets.
S57.04.where: Chat screen > + (Add attachments and tools) > Add photos & files > attach two or more files > message box: ask which file mentions a word > Send.

S57.05.note: The plan says the sandbox file-read tool is switched off until AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY are set in production; I found the gate in apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts but no user control that reads a named file.

S57.06.note: The plan says the sandbox file-write tool is switched off until AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY are set in production; I found the gate in apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts but no user control that writes a named file.

S57.07.note: The Output rows appear only for models that can create Office files.
steps: Click + and open the Output group.
Click Spreadsheet so it is checked.
Type: make a spreadsheet of three months of expenses.
Press Send and look for a file card for an .xlsx file with a download or open control.
S57.07.where: Chat screen > + (Add attachments and tools) > Output > Spreadsheet, then ask for a spreadsheet and press Send.

S57.08.note: The Output rows appear only for models that can create Office files.
steps: Click + and open the Output group.
Click Document so it is checked.
Type: write a one-page letter thanking a customer.
Press Send and look for a file card for a .docx file with a download or open control.
S57.08.where: Chat screen > + (Add attachments and tools) > Output > Document, then ask for a document and press Send.

S57.09.note: The Output rows appear only for models that can create Office files.
steps: Click + and open the Output group.
Click Presentation so it is checked.
Type: make a five-slide deck about our quarterly results.
Press Send and look for a file card for a .pptx file with a download or open control.
S57.09.where: Chat screen > + (Add attachments and tools) > Output > Presentation, then ask for a presentation and press Send.

S57.10.note: The Run code option is also in the + menu as an active chip, and the Capabilities setting 'Cloud code execution and file creation' is in Settings.
steps: Click the message box and type /code chart the first 20 prime numbers.
Press Send.
Watch the tool row: it reads 'Running code' while it runs and 'Ran code' when done.
Expand the row and check that the output of the code appears in the transcript.
S57.10.where: Chat screen > message box > type /code chart the first 20 prime numbers > Send.

S57.11.note: The plan says the sandbox shell tool is switched off until the production E2B switch is set; the + menu has a 'Run a local command' row (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx) that may be a desktop-only shell, not verified.

S57.12.note: The plan says the sandbox patch tool is switched off until the production E2B switch is set; I found no user control for targeted edits of an existing file.

S57.16.note: The Create image row shows only when the host can generate images.
steps: Click + and choose Create image, or click the message box and type /image a futuristic city at dusk.
Type or keep a short picture description.
Press Send.
Look for the generated image in the reply, under the tool row that shows image creation.
S57.16.where: Chat screen > + (Add attachments and tools) > Create image, then type a picture description > Send. Or type /image a futuristic city at dusk > Send.

labels.text: What to do with the attached image

S57.17.note: The Edit, Variation and Mask edit choices appear only in image mode after an image is attached; I did not trace how the tester enters image mode beyond the Create image row.
steps: Click + and choose Add photos & files, then attach one image.
Click the button labelled 'What to do with the attached image' and choose Edit.
Type the change you want, for example: make the sky red.
Press Send and look for the edited image in the reply.
S57.17.where: Chat screen > + (Add attachments and tools) > Add photos & files > attach one image > click the button 'What to do with the attached image' > choose Edit > type a change > Send.

S57.21.note: I did not find a visible name for the save-memory tool row, so it may show under a raw tool name.
steps: Click the message box and type: remember that I like short answers.
Press Send.
Open Settings and click Personalization, then Persistent memory.
Check that the saved fact appears in the memory list, and that Save memories from chats is on.
S57.21.where: Chat screen > message box > type 'remember that I like short answers' > Send. Then Settings > Personalization > Persistent memory.

S57.22.note: The plan says the Google Calendar OAuth client is not yet set in production, so connecting may fail; Outlook calendar needs Microsoft app credentials too.
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Find Google Calendar and connect it with your account.
Back in a chat, type: what is on my calendar today?
Press Send and look for a tool row that reads the calendar, then check the reply lists the events.
S57.22.where: Settings > Connectors > Google Calendar (connect it), then chat: ask what is on my calendar today.

S57.23.note: Use a test channel only, because the send is real.
steps: Open Settings, click Connectors, and connect Slack.
Back in a chat, type: send 'hello from QA' to a Slack channel you own.
Press Send and wait for the approval card.
Approve it and check that the tool row shows completed and the message arrives in Slack.
S57.23.where: Settings > Connectors > Slack (connect it), then chat: ask the assistant to send a message to a channel and approve it when asked.

S57.24.note: The sidebar label 'Tasks' was read from code, not confirmed on screen.
steps: In the sidebar, open Tasks and then the scheduled page.
Click New task, fill in a name and what it should do, choose a time, and save.
Check the page lists the new task under Scheduled.
Optionally, in a chat, ask the assistant to schedule a task and check it appears on the same page.
S57.24.where: Tasks > New task (scheduled page), or chat: type 'remind me every day at 9am to check the report' > Send.

S57.26.note: The assistant decides when to ask, so the tester may need to try several requests.
steps: Click the message box and type a vague request such as: plan my trip.
Press Send.
When the assistant asks a question with choices, pick one or type in 'Other answer for' the question.
Press Send answers and check that the reply continues from your answer.
S57.26.where: Chat screen > message box > send a vague request such as 'plan my trip' > look for the question card with the 'Send answers' button.

S57.28.note: Which other tools the model is told about is not visible on screen.
steps: Open Settings, click Capabilities, and find Tool access.
Choose On demand.
Back in a chat with a connected app, ask for a task that needs one of its tools.
Look for a 'Load connector tools' row in the tool timeline and check the reply uses a loaded tool.
S57.28.where: Settings > Capabilities > Tool access > On demand, then chat with a connected app and ask for a task that needs its tools.

S57.29.note: No search box was found in the UI; the keyword search runs inside the model's load call (apps/web/lib/connectors/tool-search.ts), so the tester sees only its results.
steps: Set Settings > Capabilities > Tool access to On demand.
In a chat with a connected app, ask for a task that needs a tool you did not name.
Open the tool timeline and look for the 'Load connector tools' row and the tools it lists.
S57.29.where: Visible only inside the 'Load connector tools' row of a chat reply when Tool access is On demand.

S57.30.note: The panel appears only for connectors that expose live tools.
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Open a connector that is connected.
In the panel with the heading Tools, click a tool name.
Check the description and the parameter list (name, type, required or optional) under the tool, then click Close.
S57.30.where: Settings > Connectors > [a connected connector] > capabilities panel > click a name under Tools.

S57.31.note: The Request block is missing when a call has no arguments; the card then shows 'No parameters'.
steps: Send /search latest AI news.
Click the 'Used tools' row to expand it.
Click the tool row to open its details.
Check the Request block shows the query or the JSON arguments the tool was called with.
S57.31.where: Chat screen > send a message that uses a tool (for example /search latest AI news) > click the tool row to expand it > look under Request.

S57.32.note: I did not confirm a visible elapsed-time label; durationMs is stored on each entry and passed to the card as a duration label.
steps: Send /search latest AI news and watch the reply area.
While the tool runs, look for the row text 'Running:' or 'Working...' in the timeline header.
Wait for it to finish and check the header changes away from running.
Open the row and check the status of the call.
S57.32.where: Chat screen > send a message that uses a tool > watch the tool timeline while it runs and after it finishes.

S57.33.note: The result appears in the expanded row; I did not find a separate one-line result preview on the collapsed row, so this is unverified.
steps: Send /search latest AI news and wait for the reply.
Click the 'Used tools' row to expand it.
Click the finished tool row to open its details.
Check the Response block shows the result (a short preview of the output).
S57.33.where: Chat screen > send a message that uses a tool > open the finished tool row and read the Response block.

S57.34.needs: a chat where the assistant has used a tool
S57.34.note: The tool list uses a shared card from packages/ui; the Request and Response blocks are there, but the expand and collapse control was read from code only and has not been checked in the browser.
steps: Open a chat where the assistant has used at least one tool.
Click the tool summary line, such as "Tool run complete", to open the tool list.
Click one tool row to expand it.
Look for the "Request" block (the arguments) and the "Response" block (the result) and compare with Expected.
Click the same tool row again and check that the Request and Response blocks disappear.
S57.34.where: Chat > a reply that used tools > the tool summary line (for example "Tool run complete") > click one tool row

S57.36.needs: a chat where a tool returns a very long result
S57.36.note: No control for the user was found. The stored copy is read back by the assistant through the read_tool_result tool (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-result-store.ts); the Expected phrase that the user can open it later is not confirmed by the code. Stored copies are kept for 24 hours.
steps: Ask the assistant to run a tool that returns a very long result, such as reading a long file.
Open the tool list and look for a tool row labelled "Read a stored tool result" when the assistant reads an earlier result back, and compare with Expected.
S57.36.where: Chat, when a long tool result is kept in full and trimmed from the context

S57.37.needs: a connected connector that the assistant has already called
S57.37.note: The receipt covers connectors only, not built-in tools such as search or file tools, and it does not record the input arguments or the result, which differs from Expected.
steps: Open Settings and choose Connectors.
Click a connected connector, then click "Tool permissions".
Scroll to the "Recent calls" section.
Read the rows: each shows an outcome word such as "Worked", "Failed" or "Blocked here".
Compare with Expected. The section text says "Arguments and results are never recorded", so the input part of Expected is not met by this screen.
S57.37.where: Settings > Connectors > [a connected connector] > Tool permissions > Recent calls
